1. # compose-domain v4 brief schema (PAT-002).
2. #
3. # Authoritative JSON-Schema-style declaration of the v4 brief shape.
4. # Every sub-skill validates the slice it owns against the matching
5. # section of this document. The brief grows through five conceptual
6. # passes (v0..v5) but lives as ONE YAML file at
7. # `docs/superpowers/specs/<domain>-brief.yaml`.
8. #
9. # v0  (skeleton)                  : domain + phases + personae + external_systems
10. # v1  (entity-projection)         : + entities
11. # v2  (decision-mapping)          : + decisions
12. # v3  (function-membership)       : + function
13. # v4  (ambient-trigger, optional) : + ambient
14. # v5  (sealed)                    : ready for codegen + graduate.sh
15. 
16. $schema: "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
17. $id: "https://zava.dev/compose-domain/brief.schema.yaml"
18. title: "compose-domain v4 brief"
19. type: object
20. required: [domain, phases]
21. additionalProperties: true   # v3 sections (personae, external_systems) tolerated for back-compat
22. 
23. properties:
24. 
25.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------- v0
26.   domain:
27.     type: object
28.     required: [workflow_type, prefix, display_name]
29.     additionalProperties: true
30.     properties:
31.       # Canonical kebab-case workflow_type stamped on every payload.
32.       # Drives BOTH the projection module name (underscored) AND the
33.       # Cypher file name (kebab). Phase 1 PAT-005 contract.
34.       workflow_type:
35.         type: string
36.         pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
37.       # File-name prefix used by orchestrator + activities modules
38.       # (e.g. "fleet" -> api/functions/workflows/fleet_<wt_snake>.py).
39.       prefix:
40.         type: string
41.         pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$"
42.       display_name:
43.         type: string
44.         minLength: 1
45.       # v3 back-compat:
46.       name:        { type: string }
47.       owner_role:  { type: string }
48.       description: { type: string }
49. 
50.   phases:
51.     type: array
52.     minItems: 1
53.     items:
54.       type: object
55.       required: [name, kind]
56.       additionalProperties: true
57.       properties:
58.         name: { type: string, pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$" }
59.         # Phase 4 IP4 (TASK-019): `sub_orchestrator` joins the original
60.         # three. Sub-orchestrator phases compose existing fleet domains
61.         # into a meta-workflow via Durable's `call_sub_orchestrator`.
62.         # Phase 5 (TASK-025): `graph` is the explicit opt-in for the
63.         # legacy MAF-graph shape (agent → in-graph validator → terminal,
64.         # in-process). Default for an agentic phase is `agent`, which
65.         # now generates a SEGMENT activity instead of a MAF graph. Use
66.         # `graph` only when the brief needs parallel fan-out with blind
67.         # merge, agent→validator→agent inside one activity, or saga
68.         # chains where per-node Durable round-trips are unacceptable.
69.         kind: { enum: [deterministic, agent, hitl, sub_orchestrator, graph] }
70.         persona: { type: string }
71.         external_event: { type: string }
72.         intent: { type: string }
73.         agent_skill_name: { type: string }
74.         external_systems: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
75.         # ---- sub_orchestrator-specific fields (TASK-019) ----
76.         # Required when kind == sub_orchestrator. Names the workflow_type
77.         # of the child workflow being spawned. The codegen derives the
78.         # PascalCase orchestrator class name from this (e.g.
79.         # `vendor-kyc` -> `FleetVendorKycOrchestrator` when prefix is
80.         # `fleet`); the brief may override via `target_orchestrator`.
81.         target_workflow_type: { type: string, pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$" }
82.         # Override for the auto-derived orchestrator class name. Useful
83.         # when the child domain's orchestrator does not follow the
84.         # `<Prefix><WorkflowType>Orchestrator` PascalCase convention.
85.         target_orchestrator: { type: string, pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$" }
86.         # Either a Cypher snippet (string) or a Python dict-builder
87.         # expression. The codegen embeds it as the `payload_expr` arg
88.         # to `context.call_sub_orchestrator`. If a literal dict-builder
89.         # is desired, prefix with `python:`; anything else is treated
90.         # as a Cypher template string the codegen will quote.
91.         payload_from: { type: string }
92.         # Optional grouping label. Sub-orchestrator phases sharing the
93.         # same `parallel_group` are emitted into one `context.task_all`.
94.         parallel_group: { type: string, pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$" }
95. 
96.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------- v1
97.   entities:
98.     type: array
99.     items:
100.       type: object
101.       required: [kind, ref_field, source]
102.       additionalProperties: true
103.       properties:
104.         # Must be a member of api.server.services.entity_graph._VALID_KINDS.
105.         kind: { type: string }
106.         # Dotted path inside workflow.payload that holds the entity id.
107.         ref_field: { type: string, pattern: "^payload(\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)+$" }
108.         # Free-form sub-kind label landed on the node's `kind` attr (e.g.
109.         # "vendor", "joiner", "campaign"). Optional — when absent the
110.         # node table's intrinsic `kind` column stays unset.
111.         source: { type: string }
112.         # Map of Kuzu attr column -> dotted ref into payload.
113.         attributes:
114.           type: object
115.           additionalProperties: { type: string }
116.         # Optional outbound relations from this entity.
117.         relations:
118.           type: array
119.           items:
120.             type: object
121.             required: [kind, target_ref]
122.             properties:
123.               # Must be a member of _VALID_RELS.
124.               kind: { type: string }
125.               # Either another entity's ref_field OR an entity_id literal.
126.               target_ref: { type: string }
127. 
128.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------- v2
129.   decisions:
130.     type: array
131.     items:
132.       type: object
133.       required: [phase, persona, source_event]
134.       additionalProperties: true
135.       properties:
136.         # Must match a phase in `phases` with kind == hitl.
137.         phase: { type: string }
138.         # Must match a persona role declared in `personae` (when v3
139.         # personae block is present) or under api/server/personae/.
140.         persona: { type: string }
141.         # FleetEvent type stamped on the Decision node. Defaults to
142.         # `workflow.hitl.requested` when omitted.
143.         source_event: { type: string }
144.         # Optional list of entity ref_fields the decision pertains to.
145.         decided_on_entities:
146.           type: array
147.           items: { type: string }
148.         # Optional dict of attribute key -> dotted context path. Lands
149.         # on the Decision node's `attributes` JSON blob.
150.         attributes_from_context:
151.           type: object
152.           additionalProperties: { type: string }
153. 
154.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------- v3
155.   function:
156.     # Single canonical function name. Validated against api.shared.functions
157.     # FUNCTIONS keys when importable, otherwise FUNCTIONS_PLACEHOLDER.
158.     type: string
159.     enum: [finance, hr, revenue, ops, legal, marketing, tech, data, customer-success, legacy]
160. 
161.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------- v4
162.   ambient:
163.     type: object
164.     required: [name, function, triggers, spawnable_workflow_types]
165.     additionalProperties: true
166.     properties:
167.       name: { type: string, pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$" }
168.       function:
169.         type: string
170.         enum: [finance, hr, revenue, ops, legal, marketing, tech, data, customer-success, legacy]
171.       reasoning_skill: { type: [string, "null"] }
172.       spawnable_workflow_types:
173.         type: array
174.         minItems: 1
175.         items: { type: string }
176.       triggers:
177.         type: array
178.         minItems: 1
179.         items:
180.           type: object
181.           required: [kind]
182.           properties:
183.             kind: { enum: [bus, cypher, cadence] }
184.             # bus
185.             event_type: { type: string }
186.             filter:     { type: string }
187.             # cypher
188.             pattern:        { type: string }
189.             sweep_seconds:  { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
190.             # cadence
191.             cron: { type: string }
192. 
193. 
194. # --------------------------------------------------------------------
195. # Example (full v4 brief — synthetic, for documentation only).
196. # --------------------------------------------------------------------
197. example:
198.   domain:
199.     workflow_type: vendor-kyc
200.     prefix: fleet
201.     display_name: "Vendor onboarding & KYC"
202.     description: "Vendor onboarding with KYC + UBO sweep + finance signoff."
203.   phases:
204.     - { name: vendor_intake, kind: deterministic, intent: "Capture vendor name + country." }
205.     - { name: kyc_diligence, kind: agent, agent_skill_name: kyc-diligence-checker, intent: "..." }
206.     - { name: ubo_resolver,  kind: agent, agent_skill_name: ubo-resolver, intent: "..." }
207.     - { name: finance_signoff, kind: hitl, persona: vendor_kyc_finance_bp, external_event: finance_signoff_decision }

209.     - kind: Organisation
210.       source: vendor
211.       ref_field: payload.vendor.id
212.       attributes:
213.         country:   payload.vendor.country_of_incorporation
214.         risk_band: payload.kyc.risk_band
215.   decisions:
216.     - phase: finance_signoff
217.       persona: vendor_kyc_finance_bp
218.       source_event: workflow.hitl.requested
219.       decided_on_entities: [payload.vendor.id]

1. # Vendor onboarding & KYC — third compose-domain brief.
2. #
3. # A new third-party vendor needs onboarding before any spend can be
4. # approved. Two agent phases (KYC diligence + UBO sanctions screening)
5. # followed by a finance business-partner sign-off. Introduces three new
6. # MCPs (vendor_registry, sanctions_api, adverse_media). Domain-scoped
7. # persona (vendor_kyc_finance_bp) auto-closes via decision_code.
8. 
9. domain:
10.   # v4 fields (TASK-027 backfill).
11.   workflow_type: vendor-kyc
12.   prefix: fleet
13.   # v3 fields (back-compat — v3 generators still consume `name`).
14.   name: fleet-vendor-kyc
15.   display_name: Vendor onboarding & KYC
16.   owner_role: vendor_kyc_finance_bp
17.   description: |
18.     A vendor has been proposed by a buying agency. The orchestrator
19.     captures the vendor name + country (deterministic intake). A
20.     KYC-diligence agent looks the vendor up in the registry, lists
21.     their regulatory filings, and screens the legal entity against
22.     sanctions. A UBO-resolver agent then enumerates ultimate beneficial
23.     owners, screens each one, and runs an adverse-media sweep on the
24.     top three. The finance business partner signs off (auto-approves
25.     when entity sanctions, UBO sanctions, and adverse-media verdicts
26.     are all clean). All MCPs are deterministic in-memory stubs.
27. 
28. phases:
29.   - name: vendor_intake
30.     intent: |
31.       Capture the proposed vendor name + country of incorporation +
32.       proposing agency. Pass forward.
33.     kind: deterministic
34.     external_systems: []
35. 
36.   - name: kyc_diligence
37.     intent: |
38.       Look the vendor up in the vendor registry. List their regulatory
39.       filings (last 24 months). Screen the legal entity against
40.       sanctions for both the vendor's country of incorporation and any
41.       country the vendor's filings reference.
42.     kind: agent
43.     agent_skill_name: kyc-diligence-checker
44.     external_systems: [vendor_registry, sanctions_api]
45. 
46.   - name: ubo_resolver
47.     intent: |
48.       Enumerate ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the vendor.
49.       Screen each UBO against sanctions. Run an adverse-media sweep on
50.       the top three UBOs by ownership percentage.
51.     kind: agent
52.     agent_skill_name: ubo-resolver
53.     external_systems: [vendor_registry, sanctions_api, adverse_media]
54. 
55.   - name: finance_signoff
56.     intent: |
57.       Finance business partner signs off. Approve when entity
58.       sanctions, all UBO sanctions, and the adverse-media sweep all
59.       came back clean. Otherwise reject naming the failure.
60.     kind: hitl
61.     persona: vendor_kyc_finance_bp
62.     external_systems: []
63. 
64. personae:
65.   - role: vendor_kyc_finance_bp
66.     workflow_label: Vendor onboarding & KYC
67.     decision_policy: |
68.       Approve when entity_sanctions_hits, ubo_sanctions_hits, and
69.       adverse_media_hits are all empty. Otherwise reject naming the
70.       first non-empty list in one sentence.
71.     decision_code: |
72.       kyc = (context or {}).get("kyc_diligence") or {}
73.       ubo = (context or {}).get("ubo_resolver") or {}
74.       entity_hits = kyc.get("entity_sanctions_hits") or []
75.       ubo_hits = ubo.get("ubo_sanctions_hits") or []
76.       media_hits = ubo.get("adverse_media_hits") or []
77.       if entity_hits:
78.           decision = "reject"
79.           reason = (
80.               "entity sanctions hits: "
81.               + ", ".join(str(h) for h in entity_hits[:3])
82.           )
83.       elif ubo_hits:
84.           decision = "reject"
85.           reason = (
86.               "UBO sanctions hits: "
87.               + ", ".join(str(h) for h in ubo_hits[:3])
88.           )
89.       elif media_hits:
90.           decision = "reject"
91.           reason = (
92.               "adverse media hits: "
93.               + ", ".join(str(h) for h in media_hits[:3])
94.           )
95.       else:
96.           decision = "approve"
97.           reason = "entity, UBOs and adverse-media sweep all clean"

1. # Capital expenditure (CapEx) approval — compose-domain v4 brief.
2. #
3. # Story: an employee requests funding for a capital asset (equipment,
4. # machinery, IT hardware, fit-out) costing >= GBP 1,000 with a useful
5. # life over one year. Intake captures + validates the request; a budget
6. # check reads the cost centre's remaining annual CapEx budget from the
7. # finance/ERP system; a capitalisation-review agent confirms the asset
8. # is genuinely capital, checks the depreciation schedule, and assigns a
9. # risk band; a Finance Controller approves or rejects. On approval the
10. # asset is registered in the fixed-asset register and Procurement is
11. # notified to raise the PO. Function owner: Finance.
12. #
13. # AGENT-CHOICE: the process document names "the approver" and a separate
14. # ">GBP 50k senior sign-off" without specifying roles. Per operator
15. # decision, this is modelled as a SINGLE HITL gate owned by a Finance
16. # Controller, with the >GBP 50k senior sign-off expressed as an AGT
17. # escalation chain to the CFO in data/synthetic/authority/matrix.json
18. # (see Phase 4b.8), rather than a second always-on HITL gate.
19. 
20. domain:
21.   workflow_type: capex-approval
22.   prefix: fleet
23.   display_name: Capital expenditure approval
24.   description: |
25.     An employee requests funding for a capital asset costing GBP 1,000+
26.     with a useful life over one year. The orchestrator captures and
27.     validates the request (rejecting sub-GBP-1,000 items as OpEx), reads
28.     the cost centre's remaining annual CapEx budget and year-to-date
29.     spend from the finance/ERP system, then asks a capitalisation-review
30.     agent to confirm the asset is genuinely capital, verify the
31.     depreciation schedule, and assign a risk band (low / medium / high).
32.     A Finance Controller approves when the request is in-budget,
33.     correctly capitalised, and low/medium risk; rejects when it is over
34.     budget, mis-classified, or high risk. Requests above GBP 50,000
35.     escalate to the CFO via the authority matrix. On approval the asset
36.     is registered in the fixed-asset register and Procurement is
37.     notified. The ERP + policy MCP tools are deterministic stubs.
38. 
39. phases:
40.   - name: capex_intake
41.     intent: |
42.       Capture the CapEx request: requester name, department, cost
43.       centre, asset description + category, requested amount (GBP),
44.       business justification, and expected in-service date. Reject
45.       immediately if the amount is under GBP 1,000 (that is an operating
46.       expense, handled elsewhere).
47.     kind: deterministic
48.     external_systems: []
49. 
50.   - name: budget_check
51.     intent: |
52.       Look up the requesting cost centre's remaining annual CapEx budget
53.       in the finance/ERP system for the current fiscal year and decide
54.       whether the requested amount fits within it. Also pull the
55.       department's year-to-date CapEx spend for context. Pass forward
56.       an in_budget flag, remaining_budget_gbp, and ytd_spend_gbp.
57.     kind: deterministic
58.     external_systems: []
59. 
60.   - name: capitalisation_review
61.     intent: |
62.       Check the request against the capitalisation policy. Confirm the
63.       asset category is genuinely capital (not a disguised operating
64.       cost), confirm the useful-life and depreciation schedule are
65.       correct for the category, and assign a risk band (low / medium /
66.       high) based on amount, category, and whether it exceeds the
67.       remaining budget. Flag anything that should be reclassified as
68.       OpEx. Emit is_capital, reclassify_opex, depreciation_years, and
69.       risk_band.
70.     kind: agent
71.     agent_skill_name: capitalisation-reviewer
72.     external_systems: [capitalisation_policy]
73. 
74.   - name: capex_approval
75.     intent: |
76.       Finance Controller reviews budget fit, policy compliance, and risk
77.       band, then approves or rejects. Approve when the request is
78.       in-budget, correctly capitalised, and low or medium risk. Reject
79.       with a one-line reason when it is over budget, mis-classified, or
80.       high risk. Requests above GBP 50,000 escalate to the CFO via the
81.       authority matrix before the approval is final.
82.     kind: hitl
83.     persona: capex_finance_controller
84.     external_event: capex_approval_decision
85. 
86. personae:
87.   - role: capex_finance_controller
88.     workflow_label: Capital expenditure approval
89.     decision_policy: |
90.       Approve when the request is in-budget, the asset is correctly
91.       capitalised (not flagged for OpEx reclassification), and the risk
92.       band is low or medium. Reject with a one-line reason when it is
93.       over budget, mis-classified as capital, or high risk. Requests
94.       above GBP 50,000 require CFO sign-off, handled by the authority
95.       matrix escalation chain.
96.     decision_code: |
97.       bc = (context or {}).get("budget_check") or {}
98.       cr = (context or {}).get("capitalisation_review") or {}
99.       in_budget = bc.get("in_budget")
100.       if in_budget is None:
101.           in_budget = True
102.       is_capital = cr.get("is_capital")
103.       if is_capital is None:
104.           is_capital = True
105.       reclassify = bool(cr.get("reclassify_opex"))
106.       risk = str(cr.get("risk_band") or "low").lower()
107.       if not in_budget:
108.           decision = "reject"
109.           reason = "over budget: exceeds the cost centre's remaining CapEx budget"
110.       elif reclassify or not is_capital:
111.           decision = "reject"
112.           reason = "mis-classified: should be booked as OpEx, not capitalised"
113.       elif risk == "high":
114.           decision = "reject"
115.           reason = "high risk band — rework required before approval"
116.       else:
117.           decision = "approve"
118.           reason = "in-budget, correctly capitalised, and low/medium risk"
119. 
120. external_systems:
121.   - id: capitalisation_policy
122.     mcp_tool: policy_search
123.     operations:
124.       - policy_search

414. #### When to use `kind: graph`
415. 
416. The default for an agentic phase is `kind: agent`, which generates a
417. **segment activity** (one CopilotSession loaded with all the skills
418. that segment needs; the model picks invocation order). Only opt into
419. the legacy MAF-graph shape via `kind: graph` when one of these three
420. criteria is genuinely true:
421. 
422. 1. **Parallel fan-out with blind merge.** The phase needs to fan out
423.    into N parallel executors and join them with a merge node that does
424.    not coordinate with the spawning agent. The segment loop is
425.    sequential within one CopilotSession; parallel fan-out belongs in
426.    a graph.
427. 2. **Agent → validator → agent inside one activity.** The phase needs
428.    a *bounded* retry where the second agent invocation reads the
429.    validator's structured response in-process (no Durable round-trip
430.    between agent calls). Segment retry crosses Durable activity
431.    boundaries; if the round-trip cost is unacceptable, use a graph.
432. 3. **Saga / compensation chains where Durable round-trips per node
433.    are unacceptable.** The phase composes ≥ 3 executors with
434.    compensating actions that must execute atomically with respect to
435.    each other; the orchestrator-level retry granularity is too coarse.
436. 
437. Everything else — including the common "one agentic skill produces a
438. structured output that the orchestrator hands to the next phase" case
439. — is **`kind: agent` (default segment)**. When in doubt, default to
440. segment.

17. 
18. # author-decision-mapping
19. 
20. This sub-skill encodes the persona-precedent contract: every HITL
21. phase that wants to surface "what did this persona decide last time
22. on a similar entity?" gets a Cypher template that the Phase 3
23. persona reasoning loop will run with bind params
24. ``$entity_id`` and ``$limit``.
25. 
26. ## Procedure
27. 
28. 1. **Read** the v1 brief (now carrying `entities`).
29. 2. **Propose `decisions:`.** One entry per HITL phase that should
30.    record a precedent. Schema:
31. 
32.    ```yaml
33.    decisions:
34.      - phase: <hitl-phase-name>             # must exist in phases & be kind: hitl
35.        persona: <role>                      # must exist in api/server/personae/
36.        source_event: <FleetEvent type>      # default: workflow.hitl.requested
37.        decided_on_entities: [payload.X.id]  # optional refs from entities[]
38.        attributes_from_context:             # optional context map for Decision.attributes
39.          <key>: payload.<path>
40.    ```
41. 
42. 3. **Validate.** Run `validator.py:validate(brief, ...)`. STOP on
43.    `SchemaError`.
44. 4. **Render.** For each decision, call
45.    `codegen.render_cypher(brief, decision)`. Write each to
46.    `<sandbox>/api/server/services/precedent_queries/<workflow_type>_<phase>.cypher`.
47. 5. **Hand off** to `author-function-membership`.
48. 
49. ## Cypher template (replicated from blueprint §10 decision #4)
50. 
51. ```cypher
52. // Auto-generated by compose-domain v4 author-decision-mapping codegen.
53. MATCH (d:Decision)-[:DECIDED_ON]->(e {id: $entity_id})
54. WHERE d.persona_role = '<persona>'
55.   AND d.workflow_type = '<workflow_type>'
56. RETURN d
57. ORDER BY d.decided_at DESC
58. LIMIT $limit
59. ```
60. 
61. The persona reasoning loop binds `$entity_id` from the current
62. workflow's entity ref and `$limit` from the per-call cap.
63. 
64. ## Constraints
65. 
66. - Exactly one decision per HITL phase (the dedupe triple
67.   `(workflow_id, phase, persona_role)` is enforced by Phase 1's
68.   reflector).
69. - Persona names must reference an existing folder under
70.   `api/server/personae/`.
71. - `source_event` defaults to `workflow.hitl.requested` when omitted.
72.

38.    personae). Propose **one** key.
39. 2. If two keys are plausible (e.g. employee-onboarding could be
40.    `hr` or `ops`) ask the operator. Do not guess.
41. 3. Write `function: <key>` to the brief.

60. `api/shared/functions.py` is absent (Phase 3 not merged), the patch

17. 
18. # author-ambient-trigger
19. 
20. Most domains need no ambient hook (the workflow is operator-driven
21. end-to-end). When one is needed, declare it as a single block:
22. 
23. ```yaml
24. ambient:
25.   name: <PascalCase>                     # e.g. VendorRiskWatcher
26.   function: <one of the 10 keys>         # which file to land in
27.   reasoning_skill: <kebab>               # optional GHCP skill, null = deterministic
28.   spawnable_workflow_types: [<wt>, ...]  # workflows this watcher may spawn
29.   triggers:                              # ≥ 1 of: bus | cypher | cadence
30.     - kind: bus
31.       event_type: <FleetEvent type>
32.       filter:     <Cypher-like predicate>
33.     - kind: cypher
34.       pattern:        "(node:Type {prop:value})"
35.       sweep_seconds:  3600
36.     - kind: cadence
37.       cron: "0 0 * * *"
38. ```
39. 
40. ## Procedure
41. 
42. 1. Ask the operator: "does this domain need an ambient hook?".
43. 2. If no → write nothing, return cleanly. Pipeline continues.
44. 3. If yes → propose the `ambient:` block and write it to the brief.
45. 4. Run `validator.py:validate(brief)`. STOP on `SchemaError`.
46. 5. Render with `codegen.render_ambient(brief)` → `(file_path, append_block)`.
47.    File path is `api/server/services/ambient_agents/<function>.py`.
48. 6. The codegen wraps the constructor in a sentinel block
49.    `# compose-domain:ambient:<workflow_type>` so `graduate.sh`
50.    appends idempotently.
51. 7. The constructor is guarded by `if hasattr(_module, "AmbientAgent")`
52.    so the file is import-clean before Phase 3 lands the
53.    `AmbientAgent` primitive.
54. 
55. ## Constraints
56. 
57. - `ambient.function` must equal `brief.function` (same registry
58.   ownership). Validator enforces.
59. - Every entry in `spawnable_workflow_types` must be present in the
60.   live `api.shared.domains.DOMAINS` registry OR be the brief's own
61.   `domain.workflow_type` (forward-declaration of self-spawning).
62. - Triggers form a discriminated union: each entry sets exactly one
63.   of `bus | cypher | cadence` and supplies the kind-specific keys.
64.

24. # author-entity-projection
25. 
26. This sub-skill is responsible for one thing: declaring **which graph
27. entities and relationships this workflow projects**, then emitting a
28. single Python projection module that Phase 1's
29. `api.server.services.entity_projections.PROJECTIONS` registry binds.
30. 
31. ## Procedure
32. 
33. 1. **Read the orchestrator** at
34.    `api/functions/workflows/<prefix>_<workflow_type_snake>.py`. Walk
35.    its AST to enumerate every dotted path the orchestrator stamps on
36.    the `payload` it emits. Use that as the universe of permissible
37.    `ref_field` and `attribute` paths.
38. 
39. 2. **Propose the `entities:` block.** Each entity declares:
40.    - `kind` — must be one of the seven Phase 1 node tables
41.      (`Person`, `Organisation`, `Asset`, `Money`, `Decision`, `Place`,
42.      `Period`). `Workflow` is reflector-managed; do not project it.
43.    - `ref_field` — dotted path inside `payload` (e.g.
44.      `payload.vendor.id`) holding the entity id.
45.    - `source` (optional) — sub-kind label landing on the node's
46.      `kind` attr (e.g. `vendor`, `agency`, `joiner`, `campaign`).
47.    - `attributes` (optional) — map of Kuzu column → dotted payload
48.      ref.
49.    - `relations` (optional) — list of `{kind, target_ref}` entries
50.      where `kind` is one of `_REL_TABLES` and `target_ref` is another
51.      entity's `ref_field`.
52. 
53. 3. **Validate.** Run `validator.py:validate(brief, orchestrator_path)`.
54.    On `SchemaError` (unknown kind / unresolved ref / bad rel), STOP
55.    and print the structured failure.
56. 
57. 4. **Render the projection.** Call
58.    `codegen.render_projection(brief)`. Write `(filename, body)` into
59.    the sandbox at
60.    `tools/scratch/compose-domain/<run-id>/api/server/services/entity_projections/<filename>`.
61. 
62. 5. **Hand off** to `author-decision-mapping`.
63. 
64. ## Output shape (one Python module per domain)
65. 
66. The codegen emits a module that mirrors the twelve hand-written Phase 1
67. projection modules:
68. 
69. ```python
70. """Projection: <workflow-type> (compose-domain v4 codegen)."""
71. from __future__ import annotations
72. 
73. import json
74. 
75. from api.server.services.entity_projections import (
76.     DecisionWrite, EntityWrite, RelWrite, build_decision, slug,
77. )
78. from api.shared.types import Workflow
79. 
80. WORKFLOW_TYPE = "<workflow-type>"
81. 
82. 
83. def project(workflow: Workflow) -> list[EntityWrite | RelWrite | DecisionWrite]:
84.     p = workflow.payload or {}
85.     sw = (workflow.id,)
86.     ops: list[EntityWrite | RelWrite | DecisionWrite] = []
87. 
88.     # --- Entity 0 ---
89.     <kind>_id = f"<PREFIX>-<source>-{slug(str(<ref_field>))}"
90.     ops.append(EntityWrite(
91.         kind="<Kind>", id=<kind>_id,
92.         attrs={"kind": "<source>", ...},
93.         source_workflows=sw,
94.     ))
95.     # ...
96.     return ops
97. ```
98. 
99. `build_decision(...)` is appended downstream by
100. `author-decision-mapping` — this codegen produces only `EntityWrite`
101. + `RelWrite`.
102. 
103. ## Constraints
104. 
105. - The function MUST be named `project` (Phase 1 PAT-005). The module
106.   MUST expose `WORKFLOW_TYPE = "<workflow-type>"` so the registry can
107.   bind it.
108. - Imports MUST be limited to the allow-list above; the validator
109.   enforces this on the rendered output.
110. - ID prefix convention (matches Phase 1):
111.   `Person → PERSON-`, `Organisation → ORG-`, `Asset → ASSET-`,
112.   `Money → MONEY-`, `Decision → DEC-`, `Place → PLACE-`,
113.   `Period → PERIOD-`.
114. 
115. ## Failure handling
116. 
117. Validation failure aborts the pipeline. Re-author the brief.

2. """
3. The single ExpenseClaim generator orchestration — one POC1 expense claim end-to-end.
4. 
5. 7 phases per spec §4.1:
6.   Intake -> Classify -> Validate Receipt -> Route -> Notify -> Arbitrate -> Audit
7. 
8. HITL gates:
9.   - Phase 5 (Notify, Red path only) waits for the `justification` external event
10.   - Phase 6 (Arbitrate) waits for the `reviewer_decision` external event
11. 
12. Sync generator per the Azure Durable Functions Python convention. Phases 3-7
13. call activity triggers that exist registered in function_app.py; the activity
14. bodies for Phases 3-7 will be wired progressively over Days 7-10 / Week 3.
15. """
16. from __future__ import annotations
17. from collections.abc import Generator
18. from typing import Any
19. 
20. import azure.durable_functions as df
21. 
22. from api.shared.constants import (
23.     DECISION_REJECTED,
24.     JUSTIFICATION_TIMEOUT,
25.     REVIEWER_DECISION_TIMEOUT,
26. )
27. 
28. 
29. def expense_claim_orchestration(context: df.DurableOrchestrationContext) -> Generator[Any, Any, dict]:
30.     """Orchestrate the 7 expense-compliance phases for one claim."""
31.     input_dict = context.get_input() or {}
32.     workflow_id = input_dict.get("workflow_id", "?")
33.     # Stamped on every checkpoint payload so internal_durable_event can
34.     # populate its _workflow_types cache and forward `workflow_type` onto
35.     # every downstream FleetEvent. Without this, recordings come out
36.     # tagged "unknown-..." and the page can't resolve the domain on
37.     # replay. Mirrors the pattern the generated travel domain uses.
38.     workflow_type = input_dict.get("type", "expense-claim")
39.     enriched = {**input_dict, "instance_id": context.instance_id}
40. 
41.     yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
42.         "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
43.         "kind": "workflow.started", "payload": {"workflow_type": workflow_type},
44.     })
45. 
46.     # Phase 1: Intake & Normalise
47.     intake_result = yield context.call_activity("intake_activity_trigger", enriched)
48.     enriched = {**enriched, "intake": intake_result}
49. 
50.     # Phase 2: Classify (R/A/G)
51.     classify_result = yield context.call_activity("classify_activity_trigger", enriched)
52.     enriched = {**enriched, "classify": classify_result}
53. 
54.     # Phase 3: Validate Receipt — wired in Day 7
55.     receipt_result = yield context.call_activity("receipt_activity_trigger", enriched)
56.     enriched = {**enriched, "receipt": receipt_result}
57. 
58.     # Phase 4: Route by Verdict — wired in Day 9
59.     route_result = yield context.call_activity("route_activity_trigger", enriched)
60.     enriched = {**enriched, "route": route_result}
61. 
62.     verdict = (classify_result or {}).get("verdict", "amber")
63. 
64.     # Phase 5: Notify (Red path only) + Phase 6: Arbitrate — wired in Day 10 / Week 3
65.     if verdict == "red":
66.         notify_result = yield context.call_activity("notify_activity_trigger", enriched)
67.         enriched = {**enriched, "notify": notify_result}
68. 
69.         yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
70.             "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
71.             "kind": "suspended",
72.             # wait_kind: external_party — the claim submitter (employee) has
73.             # to justify. The SSC operator queue shouldn't care; they only
74.             # see this if it ages past SLA.
75.             "payload": {
76.                 "reason": "awaiting_justification",
77.                 "wait_kind": "external_party",
78.                 "phase": "Notify",
79.                 "workflow_type": workflow_type,
80.                 # Persona-responder contract: who closes this gate, on what
81.                 # event, with what context. The claim_submitter persona
82.                 # synthesises a plausible justification from the parked
83.                 # claim record (mirrors what simulate_justification did
84.                 # manually).
85.                 "persona": "claim_submitter",
86.                 "external_event": "justification",
87.                 "context": {
88.                     "claim": enriched.get("claim"),
89.                     "classify": enriched.get("classify"),
90.                     "receipt": enriched.get("receipt"),
91.                     "route": enriched.get("route"),
92.                 },
93.             },
94.         })
95. 
96.         justification_event = context.wait_for_external_event("justification")
97.         timeout_event = context.create_timer(context.current_utc_datetime + JUSTIFICATION_TIMEOUT)
98.         winner = yield context.task_any([justification_event, timeout_event])
99. 
100.         if winner == timeout_event:
101.             yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
102.                 "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
103.                 "kind": "workflow.completed", "payload": {"status": "timeout"}
104.             })
105.             return {"status": "timeout", "phase": "Notify"}
106.         timeout_event.cancel()
107. 
108.         justification = justification_event.result
109.         enriched["justification"] = justification
110. 
111.         yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
112.             "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
113.             "kind": "resumed", "payload": {"justification": justification}
114.         })
115. 
116.         arbitrate_result = yield context.call_activity("arbitrate_activity_trigger", enriched)
117.         enriched = {**enriched, "arbitrate": arbitrate_result}
118. 
119.         yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
120.             "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
121.             "kind": "suspended",
122.             # wait_kind: operator_review — SSC reviewer must accept/reject.
123.             # This goes on the operator queue and ages against our SLA.
124.             "payload": {
125.                 "reason": "awaiting_reviewer",
126.                 "wait_kind": "operator_review",
127.                 "phase": "Arbitrate",
128.                 "workflow_type": workflow_type,
129.                 # Persona-responder contract: ssc_reviewer applies the
130.                 # accept/reject rule against the parked arbitrate output.
131.                 "persona": "ssc_reviewer",
132.                 "external_event": "reviewer_decision",
133.                 "context": {
134.                     "claim": enriched.get("claim"),
135.                     "classify": enriched.get("classify"),
136.                     "justification": enriched.get("justification"),
137.                     "arbitrate": enriched.get("arbitrate"),
138.                 },
139.             },
140.         })
141. 
142.         decision_event = context.wait_for_external_event("reviewer_decision")
143.         timeout_event = context.create_timer(context.current_utc_datetime + REVIEWER_DECISION_TIMEOUT)
144.         winner = yield context.task_any([decision_event, timeout_event])
145. 
146.         if winner == timeout_event:
147.             yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
148.                 "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
149.                 "kind": "workflow.completed", "payload": {"status": "timeout"}
150.             })
151.             return {"status": "timeout", "phase": "Arbitrate"}
152.         timeout_event.cancel()
153. 
154.         decision = decision_event.result
155.         decision_type = (
156.             (decision.get("decision") or "") if isinstance(decision, dict) else ""
157.         ).lower()
158. 
159.         if decision_type in DECISION_REJECTED:
160.             yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
161.                 "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
162.                 "kind": "workflow.rejected",
163.                 "payload": {
164.                     "by": decision.get("resolved_by") if isinstance(decision, dict) else None,
165.                     "reason": "reviewer rejected",
166.                 },
167.             })
168.             return {"status": "rejected", "phase": "Arbitrate", "decision": decision}
169. 
170.         enriched["reviewer_decision"] = decision
171. 
172.         yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
173.             "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
174.             "kind": "resumed", "payload": {"decision": decision}
175.         })
176. 
177.     # Phase 7: Audit — wired in Week 3
178.     audit_result = yield context.call_activity("audit_activity_trigger", enriched)
179.     enriched = {**enriched, "audit": audit_result}
180. 
181.     yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {
182.         "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
183.         "kind": "workflow.completed", "payload": {}
184.     })
185. 
186.     return {
187.         "status": "completed",
188.         "verdict": verdict,
189.         "intake": intake_result,
190.         "classify": classify_result,
191.         "receipt": receipt_result,
192.         "route": route_result,
193.         "audit": audit_result,
194.     }
195.

54. def _payload_to_get(ref: str) -> str:
55.     """Translate a ``payload.<a>.<b>.<c>`` ref to a Python expression
56.     that reads from ``p`` with `.get` chains and a sensible default.
57.     """
58.     if not ref.startswith("payload."):
59.         raise ValueError(f"ref must start with 'payload.': {ref!r}")
60.     parts = ref.split(".")[1:]
61.     if len(parts) == 1:
62.         return f'p.get({parts[0]!r})'
63.     expr = f'(p.get({parts[0]!r}) or {{}})'
64.     for k in parts[1:-1]:
65.         expr = f'({expr}.get({k!r}) or {{}})'
66.     expr = f'{expr}.get({parts[-1]!r})'
67.     return expr

71.     if not attrs:

74.              for k, v in attrs.items()]

2. """
3. TrackedExecutor: wraps one of our async `execute(input: dict) -> dict` functions as a real
4. MAF Executor that emits webhook events before/after invocation and forwards the merged
5. input+output dict to the next node.
6. 
7. `executor_type` is one of "deterministic" | "agent" | "validator" -- it labels the event
8. emission so the UI can render type-specific icons.
9. """
10. from __future__ import annotations
11. import time
12. from typing import Awaitable, Callable
13. from agent_framework import Executor, Workflow, WorkflowBuilder, WorkflowContext, handler
14. from opentelemetry import trace
15. from opentelemetry.trace import Status, StatusCode
16. from api.functions.webhook import emit
17. 
18. 
19. ExecuteFn = Callable[[dict], Awaitable[dict]]
20. 
21. _tracer = trace.get_tracer("zava.graphs.executor")
22. 
23. 
24. class TrackedExecutor(Executor):
25.     """Wraps an async execute(input)->dict function. On each invocation, emits webhooks
26.     and forwards the merged dict to the next node."""
27. 
28.     def __init__(self, *, id: str, name: str, executor_type: str, fn: ExecuteFn):
29.         super().__init__(id=id)
30.         self._name = name
31.         self._executor_type = executor_type
32.         self._fn = fn
33. 
34.     @handler(input=dict, output=dict)
35.     async def process(self, input: dict, ctx: WorkflowContext) -> None:
36.         wid = input.get("workflow_id", "?")
37.         iid = input.get("instance_id")
38.         phase = input.get("phase")
39.         t0 = time.time()
40.         await emit(wid, iid, "executor.invoked", {
41.             "name": self._name, "type": self._executor_type, "stage": "start"
42.         })
43.         with _tracer.start_as_current_span(f"executor.{self._name}") as span:
44.             span.set_attribute("zava.workflow.id", str(wid))
45.             if iid is not None:
46.                 span.set_attribute("zava.workflow.instance_id", str(iid))
47.             if phase is not None:
48.                 span.set_attribute("zava.workflow.phase", str(phase))
49.             span.set_attribute("zava.executor.type", self._executor_type)
50.             span.set_attribute("zava.executor.name", self._name)
51.             if self._executor_type == "agent":
52.                 # Each executor name corresponds to a skill, which is its
53.                 # own agent in the AGT design. Tag the span with the
54.                 # executor name so audit/Foundry can attribute by agent.
55.                 span.set_attribute("gen_ai.agent.name", self._name)
56. 
57.             try:
58.                 result = await self._fn(input)
59.             except Exception as ex:
60.                 span.record_exception(ex)
61.                 span.set_status(Status(StatusCode.ERROR, str(ex)))
62.                 await emit(wid, iid, "executor.invoked", {
63.                     "name": self._name, "type": self._executor_type, "stage": "error",
64.                     "error": str(ex), "duration_ms": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000)
65.                 })
66.                 raise
67. 
68.             if self._executor_type == "validator" and result.get("ok") is False:
69.                 reason = result.get("blocked_reason") or result.get("missing") or "validation failed"
70.                 span.set_status(Status(StatusCode.ERROR, str(reason)))
71.                 span.add_event("validator.blocked", {"reason": str(reason)})
72. 
73.         await emit(wid, iid, "executor.invoked", {
74.             "name": self._name, "type": self._executor_type, "stage": "complete",
75.             "duration_ms": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000)
76.         })
77.         # Merge input + result so downstream nodes have full context
78.         merged = {**input, **result}
79.         # If a validator failed, emit dedicated event
80.         if self._executor_type == "validator" and result.get("ok") is False:
81.             await emit(wid, iid, "validator.blocked", {
82.                 "name": self._name, "reason": result.get("blocked_reason") or result.get("missing") or "validation failed"
83.             })
84.             # Still forward -- orchestration generator decides what to do with ok=False
85.         await ctx.send_message(merged)
86.

88. class TerminalExecutor(Executor):
89.     """Final node in a graph: yields the accumulated dict as the workflow output."""
90. 
91.     def __init__(self, *, id: str = "terminal"):
92.         super().__init__(id=id)
93. 
94.     @handler(input=dict, workflow_output=dict)
95.     async def process(self, input: dict, ctx: WorkflowContext) -> None:
96.         await ctx.yield_output(input)
97.

99. def build_linear_workflow(
100.     nodes: list[tuple[str, str, str, ExecuteFn]],
101.     *,
102.     terminal_id: str = "terminal",
103. ) -> Workflow:
104.     """Build a linear graph: ``nodes[0] -> nodes[1] -> ... -> terminal``.
105. 
106.     Each node is ``(id, name, executor_type, fn)``. Collapses the
107.     TrackedExecutor + WorkflowBuilder boilerplate that every graph builder
108.     in this package otherwise repeats by hand.
109.     """
110.     chain: list[Executor] = [
111.         TrackedExecutor(id=node_id, name=name, executor_type=executor_type, fn=fn)
112.         for node_id, name, executor_type, fn in nodes
113.     ]
114.     chain.append(TerminalExecutor(id=terminal_id))
115.     builder = WorkflowBuilder(start_executor=chain[0])
116.     for src, dst in zip(chain, chain[1:]):
117.         builder = builder.add_edge(src, dst)
118.     return builder.build()

25. # them into api/shared/constants.py and rewrites this file's import.
26. def fleet_vendor_kyc_orchestration(context: df.DurableOrchestrationContext) -> Generator[Any, Any, dict]:
27.     """Orchestrate the 4 Vendor onboarding & KYC phases for one workflow."""
28.     input_dict = context.get_input() or {}
29.     workflow_id = input_dict.get("workflow_id", "?")
30.     # v3 substrate-fix contract: stamp workflow_type on every checkpoint
31.     # payload so internal_durable_event populates its _workflow_types
32.     # cache and forwards `workflow_type` onto every downstream FleetEvent.
33.     # Without this, recordings come out tagged unknown-... and SSE events
34.     # arrive with domain=null.

37. 
38.     yield context.call_activity("checkpoint_activity_trigger", {

43. 
44.     # Phase 1: Vendor Intake (deterministic)
45.     vendor_intake_result = yield context.call_activity(

47.     )

64.         "workflow_id": workflow_id, "instance_id": context.instance_id,
65.         "kind": "suspended",
66.         "payload": {
67.             "reason": "awaiting_finance_signoff",
68.             "phase": "finance_signoff",
69.             "wait_kind": "operator_review",
70.             "workflow_type": workflow_type,
71.             # Persona-responder contract: tell the responder which persona

74.             "persona": "vendor_kyc_finance_bp",

76.             "context": {
77.                 "ubo_resolver": enriched.get("ubo_resolver"),

79.             },
80.         },

92.                         "workflow_type": workflow_type},

95.     timeout_event.cancel()

2. name: receipt-validator
3. description: Cross-validate an expense claim's receipt image against the claim's structured fields (vendor, amount, date, line item). Detect six mismatch flavours: correct, wrong-amount, wrong-date, wrong-vendor, missing-line-item, missing-receipt.
4. allowed-tools: claim_get_structured, ocr_extract
5. ---
6. 
7. You validate receipt images against expense-claim records.
8. 
9. ## Inputs
10. 
11. The user prompt names a claim id. The session may also include the receipt image as a multimodal attachment.
12. 
13. ## Step 0: Extract via Document Intelligence
14. 
15. Before inspecting the image, call:
16. 
17. ```
18. ocr_extract(document_id=claim_id, model="prebuilt-receipt")
19. ```
20. 
21. The structured fields it returns (`merchantName`, `total`, `transactionDate`, `items[]`) are your **authoritative read** of the receipt. Use them as primary evidence, with the attached image as a sanity check. Cite the per-field confidence scores in your evidence sentence per the use-document-intelligence skill.
22. 
23. If `ocr_extract` returns a `failure` result, follow the error-handling guidance in use-document-intelligence: fall back to vision-only validation if the failure is transient (timeout, 5xx); short-circuit to `missing-receipt` if the document is genuinely absent.
24. 
25. Procedure:
26. 
27. 1. Call `claim_get_structured(claim_id)` to load the claim's structured fields: vendor, amount, currency, submitted_at (date), category, attendees.
28. 2. Inspect the attached receipt image. Read off the receipt's vendor name, total amount + currency, transaction date, and itemised lines.
29. 3. Compare the receipt against the structured claim fields. Decide one mismatch flavour:
30.    - **correct** — receipt matches the claim on vendor, amount (within ±2% rounding), date, and there's at least one line item consistent with the claim's category.
31.    - **wrong-amount** — receipt total differs from the claim amount by more than 2%.
32.    - **wrong-date** — receipt date is more than 30 days before/after the claim's `submitted_at`.
33.    - **wrong-vendor** — receipt vendor name doesn't reasonably match `claim.vendor`. ("NOT-Côte Brasserie" or a totally different name → wrong-vendor.)
34.    - **missing-line-item** — receipt total/header is fine but no itemised lines visible, or no line resembles the claim category (e.g. claim is meals but receipt only has "Service charge").
35.    - **missing-receipt** — no receipt was attached (the agent will signal this explicitly).
36. 
37. If the receipt is absent (the agent passes `flavour: "missing-receipt"` in the prompt), short-circuit to that verdict without inspection.
38. 
39. ## Output
40. 
41. Return exactly one JSON object, no prose:
42. 
43. ```json
44. {
45.   "verdict": "match" | "mismatch",
46.   "flavour": "correct" | "wrong-amount" | "wrong-date" | "wrong-vendor" | "missing-line-item" | "missing-receipt",
47.   "evidence": "1-3 sentences. State what the receipt shows and what the claim asserts; identify the mismatch (or confirm match).",
48.   "confidence": 0.0,
49.   "field_confidences": {
50.     "merchantName": 0.0,
51.     "total": 0.0,
52.     "transactionDate": 0.0
53.   }
54. }
55. ```
56. 
57. Rules:
58. - `verdict` is `"match"` iff `flavour == "correct"`.
59. - `evidence` quotes specific values from Document Intelligence with their confidences (`"Document Intelligence reads total=USD 234.50 (conf 0.97)"`) and the claim (`"claim asserts USD 156.33"`). Never guess fields you can't see.
60. - `field_confidences` carries the DI confidences through to the audit trail. Copy them verbatim from the `documents[].fields.*.confidence` values you read.
61. - If the image is unreadable or absent, return `flavour: "missing-receipt"` (or `flavour: "missing-line-item"` if the header is visible but the body is illegible).
62. - The skill is non-destructive — never propose corrections to the claim record. Just classify the mismatch.
